scenes.headline: count()
scenes.subtitle: Counting the rows in a DataFrame.
scenes.narration: The count action returns the total number of rows in a DataFrame, triggering a full pass over the data.

scenes.headline: What count does
items: Returns the row count as a single number
Is an action that scans every partition
Often used to validate pipeline outputs
Can be slow because it reads the whole dataset
scenes.narration: Count returns the total number of rows as a single number. It is an action that scans every partition, is often used to validate pipeline outputs, and can be slow because it must read the whole dataset.

scenes.headline: Counting after a filter
scenes.code:
total = df.count()
errors = df.filter(df.status == "ERROR").count()
print(f"{errors} errors out of {total}")
scenes.narration: We count the total rows, then count only the error rows after filtering, and print both. Each count is a separate action, so Spark runs the plan twice here — something to keep in mind when counts are expensive.

scenes.text: Each count re-runs the plan — cache the DataFrame if you count it repeatedly.
scenes.narration: Since each count re-runs the plan, cache the DataFrame first if you intend to count or reuse it several times.
